findings.body: Raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods build_occurrence_and_event_data, counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, crashing any detector processing that reaches this handler.
findings.failure_mode: Runtime TypeError on instantiation of a class that is exported and wired up as a live detector_handler.
findings.impact: Raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods build_occurrence_and_event_data, counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, crashing any detector processing that reaches this handler.
findings.root_cause: Base class was switched from DetectorHandler (with a concrete evaluate() stub) to StatefulDetectorHandler (which now declares additional abstract methods including the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data), but the subclass body was reduced to `pass`, leaving all abstract methods unimplemented.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement the required abstract members (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data) on MetricAlertDetectorHandler before switching its base class to StatefulDetectorHandler, or keep a minimal concrete implementation until those are ready.
findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler cannot be instantiated: abstract methods not implemented
findings.trigger: Any code that accesses Detector.detector_handler for a Detector whose type resolves to MetricAlertFire (slug 'metric_alert_fire'), which calls group_type.detector_handler(self) and thus instantiates MetricAlertDetectorHandler.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch changes MetricAlertDetectorHandler to inherit from StatefulDetectorHandler (which declares abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data per lines 142-170 in detector.py) but the class body is just 'pass' with no implementations. StatefulDetectorHandler is marked abc.ABC. Python will raise TypeError on instantiation. The detector_handler property at line 86 of detector.py calls group_type.detector_handler(self), which would instantiate this class.

pr.body:
This adds a hook that can be implemented to produce an occurrence specific to the detector that is subclassing the StatefulDetector.

Also change the signature of evaluate to return a dict keyed by groupkey instead of a list. This helps avoid the chance of duplicate results for the same group key.

raw_findings.body: Tests never validate that the produced occurrence/event data actually reflects the triggering value, so a real regression in how build_occurrence_and_event_data incorporates `value` into the occurrence would not be caught by these tests.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent loss of test coverage for value-dependent occurrence construction logic.
raw_findings.impact: Tests never validate that the produced occurrence/event data actually reflects the triggering value, so a real regression in how build_occurrence_and_event_data incorporates `value` into the occurrence would not be caught by these tests.
raw_findings.root_cause: The newly added helper build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts a `value` parameter that is never referenced in its body, so callers can pass arbitrary/mismatched values without affecting test outcomes.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the unused `value` parameter from build_mock_occurrence_and_event or use it in constructing evidence_data/occurrence fields so tests actually assert on it, and pass the real evaluated value from each test call site.

finding.verifier_reason: The candidate claims the 'value' parameter in build_mock_occurrence_and_event is unused, weakening tests. However, this is a test helper function, and unused parameters in test mocks are common and intentional design choices to match production signatures. The parameter exists to match the abstract method signature of build_occurrence_and_event_data. This is not a defect - it's a deliberate mock that doesn't need to use all parameters. The claim of 'test gap' is speculative without evidence of actual regression risk.
